mechanics.control_flow: 9 conditional branches, all with absolute targets inside 0x00a850d0..0x00a851bf, plus one intra-procedural JMP at 00a85129 that skips the PUSH 0x0. Two return sites, both RET 0x4. No loop, no switch, no computed jump, no exception handling.
mechanics.bit_tests: each of the four is (word >> k) & 1 with the shift immediate read off the listing's own SHR: bit 2 at 00a850ef, bit 4 at 00a85106, bit 6 at 00a85115, bit 1 at 00a8513d. Bit 1 selects BETWEEN two dispatches (0x0c when set, the 0x8518c arm when clear); bit 6 is a modifier of the bit-4 arm's second argument, never an arm by itself; bits 0, 3, 5 and 7 are never tested.
mechanics.arm_decision: the three transfers are conditionally nested, not sequential: bit 2 at 00a850f5 skips to 00a850fe, bit 4 at 00a8510c skips to 00a85130, and bit 1 at 00a85142 skips to 00a8518c. Falling out of the bit-1-SET arm reaches 00a8515c, so at most three transfers occur and the fourth is mutually exclusive with the third.
mechanics.exact_find_not_lower_bound: the argument ORDER of the three two-argument transfers is read from the pushes backwards, not assumed: 00a85128 PUSH EDI then 00a8512d PUSH EAX, likewise 00a85158/00a85159 and 00a851ae/00a851af. The first pushed word is therefore at the HIGHER address [ESP+4].
mechanics.not_modelled: what the four callees do, and whether they preserve EAX or XMM0. Three of the four results are discarded by the body; only the 0x10 site's EAX is used.
mechanics.globals: TWO, both read-only and both in .rdata, both read out of the image rather than guessed: 0x01485720 (RVA 0x1085720, file bytes 00 00 80 3f, i.e. +1.0f) is the DIVIDEND at 00a85176/00a8517e, and 0x01485378 (RVA 0x1085378, file bytes 00 00 00 00, i.e. +0.0f) is the COMISS threshold at 00a85191. The second reading is corroborated from inside the body: 00a85198 tests the same float against that word as 00a85171 tests it against the XMM1 that 00a8515c just zeroed. Neither address is written.
mechanics.return_register_is_not_the_stored_regist: 00a8516c loads the carrier's float into XMM0; 00a8517e divides INTO XMM1; 00a85182 stores XMM1 on the receiver. So the value the caller receives is the carrier's float and NOT its reciprocal, while the receiver gets the reciprocal. The reconstruction keeps two separate locals for the two registers and the model test drives a scale of four so the two numbers differ by a factor of sixteen.
mechanics.receiver_writes: five dword-or-wider stores in total: one byte at 0x14, two MOVSS stores at 0x1c and 0x20, one MOVSS store at 0x18, and two dword stores at 0x68. The model test checks the WHOLE receiver byte for byte after a run, not only the fields it reasons about.

return_semantics.value: the carrier's float at displacement 0x10, loaded into XMM0 at 00a8516c (or at 00a8518c on the early-return path), which is what the caller receives on every path that writes XMM0
return_semantics.untouched_path: on the guard path (00a850d7 taken) the body reaches 00a85188 with XMM0 never written, so the caller receives whatever XMM0 held on entry. The reconstruction returns the incoming register contents unchanged, exposed as set_xmm0_bits/xmm0_bits so the model test can plant a sentinel and observe the pass-through. return_semantics.lifetime: not applicable: a 4-byte value in a register

unresolved_questions: RETURN SEMANTICS is a WARN and cannot be made a PASS from the source side. The canonical ABI record's own token is the machine phrase float_or_x87_in_XMM0 (abi_derived.value.abi.return_semantics, with abi.value.return.type = null and abi.value.return.void_possible = false at confidence APPROXIMATION). No C++ spelling can equal that string, so the string-agreement arm reports a rename however the return type is written. The declaration made here is float, which is TRUE OF THE LISTING: XMM0 is the recorded return register and the body writes it with a four-byte MOVSS at 00a8516c and 00a8518c and a four-byte DIVSS at 00a8517e, all single-precision four-byte scalars. Option (b) of the wave-1 rule -- declaring void -- was rejected because the bytes demonstrably produce a value on every path that writes XMM0. No typedef was invented after the machine phrase, because that is a validator hack and not a claim.

GLOBALS is a WARN and is an evidence ceiling, not a defect. The complete 81-instruction listing names two data-segment addresses (0x01485720 and 0x01485378) and the xref export carries no data-reference edge type at all -- every edge in it is direct-call, computed-call, thunk or external -- so there is no second machine side to corroborate a read/write mode against. The listing's own text fixes the mode for both: both are the source operand of a MOVSS, and neither address is ever a destination. The constants are declared in the header with their addresses and their transcribed values, and the model test overwrites both to show they are reads rather than baked-in literals. Omitting the stores was not an option, because that would be a falsification of the body.

EVIDENCE COVERAGE is a WARN and is a property of the pack, not of the reconstruction: 9 of 17 static evidence categories are available for this target. The missing ones are callees_dependencies, callers_dependencies, contradictions, decompilation, external_callees, globals, runtime, semantic_hypotheses and types.

Does the transfer at 00a851b0 clobber XMM0? On the early-return path at 00a851b7 the value the caller receives is whatever XMM0 held after that transfer, and 00a8518c is the last write the listing shows. Whether a callee preserves XMM0 across the call is a property of the CALLEE's signature, which this listing cannot show, so the model returns the pre-call value (the carrier's float) and the model test asserts only that. The clobber case is deliberately left unasserted in either direction.

Are the three two-argument callees callee-cleanup? The body never adjusts ESP after 00a8512e, 00a8515a or 00a851b0, so a callee that did NOT pop its two words would leave the stack inconsistent for the rest of the function. That is an inference from an absence, not an observation of any callee, and it is recorded in the header at the typedefs rather than presented as a fact.

What owns the dispatch table? The four targets are four-byte words at displacements 0x18, 0x1c, 0x0c and 0x10 of a table reached by reading the dispatch object's lead dword, and the machine's own dispatch classifier calls all four sites VTABLE_SLOT. Nothing in this body fixes whether that table is a vtable, a callback array, or a dispatch record of some other kind, and the same instruction sequence would be produced by any of them. The displacements are claimed; the ownership is not, and the model test asserts only the addresses, the order and the argument order.

What are the four callees, semantically? Three of the four results are discarded by the body and the fourth is stored and signed-tested, so this target constrains their signatures and nothing else. No claim is made about what they compute.

What is the semantic role of the receiver, the carrier, the flag word's four bits, the guard byte, the three receiver floats and the word at receiver+0x68? This listing names none of them, the Spore-ModAPI SDK resolves no symbol for 0x00a850d0 (function_identity.types is empty, ghidra_function.sdk_name is null), and the binary carries no MSVC RTTI, so the class this function is slot 2 of cannot be named from this evidence. The Editor cluster label on this target comes from the triage queue and is NOT a claim made here.

validation.compile_gate: clean under -Wall -Wextra -Werror; the header also compiles alone (a translation unit that only includes it)
validation.model_test: 429 checks, 0 failures, exit 0. Twelve cases: A the guard byte; B the null dispatch pointer; C all eight flag-bit positions plus three two-bit combinations; D argument order, halfword width, address-argument identity, DIVSS order and the return register; E the COMISS polarity at both comparison sites including the unordered case plus both .rdata words overwritten; F six signed-compare results including 0x7fffffff and 0x80000000; G write ordering sampled from inside each callee; H the register argument of all four transfers; I the four separate reads of receiver+0x0c, driven by two mid-run carrier replacements; J the four separate reads of receiver+0x10, driven by two mid-run dispatch-object replacements; K no write outside the receiver and the popped stack word never read; L an exhaustive sweep of the low nibble of the flag word against a predicted transfer sequence.

mutation_checking.method: decoys and mid-run writes rather than a mutation harness. Every word the model could fetch is planted: the real dispatch table carries a decoy observer in every slot except the four the machine fetches, and a fully-observed decoy table is planted on the receiver, on the dispatch object, on the carrier and at the table's own lead word, so a wrong base or a wrong pointer level CALLS a decoy instead of crashing. The two halfword push values are given distinct patterns and the carrier's word at 0xa8 is poisoned in its high half, so a swapped pair and a dword-for-halfword read are both visible. The observers are additionally given the power to rewrite receiver+0x0c and receiver+0x10 mid-run, which is the only way to refute a model that caches either pointer.
results: wrong receiver or wrong pointer level: a decoy transfer runs, and the decoy counter reports it
wrong slot displacement (0x04, 0x08, 0x14, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28 or 0x2c): a decoy transfer runs
wrong bit index in either direction: the predicted transfer sequence for the affected flag word does not match
wrong branch polarity: the negative float, +0.0f, -0.0f and NaN cases take the wrong side of 00a85174 and 00a85198
signed rewritten as unsigned: 0x80000000 releases the guard byte under the wrong reading
swapped stack arguments: the two patterns are exchanged and the check names which one is wrong
dword read at carrier+0xa8: the poisoned high half reaches the callee
DIVSS operand order reversed: receiver+0x18 becomes 4 instead of 0.25 for a scale of four
returning the stored reciprocal instead of the carrier's float: the return-value check names it
00a85133 placed after either transfer, or the result store placed before its transfer: the receiver sample taken inside the callee does not match
caching receiver+0x0c: the replaced run produces two transfers instead of three, and the later halfword, arguments and reciprocal come from the wrong carrier
caching receiver+0x10: the later transfers go through the original table instead of the replacement
a hard-coded .rdata value: overwriting the threshold word or the dividend does not change the outcome
a two-level or three-level pointer chase in the wrong direction: a decoy transfer runs
mutation_checking.survivors: two residual limits, both stated rather than papered over. (1) The decoy observers are declared with two stack parameters, so a model that mis-dispatched to a decoy at the ZERO-argument site would balance the model's stack wrongly; the decoy is counted and reported before that matters, and a refutation case may therefore terminate the binary rather than print. (2) The XMM0 pass-through on the guard path is checked with a sentinel word, which distinguishes a pass-through from a manufactured value but cannot distinguish a pass-through from a caller's-register-relative computation that happens to agree.
mutation_checking.known_limits: the test cannot refute a callee-cleanup reading, because the body itself would be self-inconsistent under one; and it deliberately does not assert the XMM0 clobber case at 00a851b0, which the listing cannot settle.
